A shared cluster seems easy. But a job asking for a whole GPU waits about nine hours. Only seven of the cards have eighty gigabytes. A small share of a card starts in seconds, but fits only small trainings.

An agent building, training, fixing and retrying needs dozens of rounds daily. A queue makes each round cost hours. On the workstation, one training fold on an A5000 takes about twenty five minutes. Rounds cost minutes.
Second, the data. Clara runs on the workstation, so patient images never leave it. A cloud model cannot see them. Clara reads every scan and mask, and runs the model on the whole cohort.
Local is a route, not a permission. The data agreement decides if an AI system may process a dataset. A forbidding clause binds the local model too. If allowed, local keeps data inside.
So the workstation is not a smaller cluster. It is the only place where the loop is fast and data may stay. That is why we do not just use the cluster.
